log.msg: Deliverable 1 (open-mic mode) built: Dictate.js gets mode:"open" — hides the "stop after a pause" checkbox, never writes a committed sentence into the target box (push_to_target short-circuits), and draw_caption() renders every settled sentence as its own appended line instead of one truncated blob. Wired into TalkMic (talk/page.js) and ComposerMic (ai2/compose.js).

Mixed-clock fix (the 'Also' item): Dictate's and ComposerMic's log_prompt() no longer send `at` to Servex — Log.append()'s `{at: stamp(), ...entry}` only stamps its own local-offset clock when the entry arrives without one, and a client ISO string was silently overriding it. The dev-server fallback path (Servex down) still stamps its own `at` since that path has no clock of its own.

Deliverable 2 (route+id continuation): assistant.md documents a `correction` route and 'pass the same id back to evolve a card'; Assistant.js's tool schema documents `id`/`re` as callable params (the code already honored them, it just never told the model they existed). PROVEN live against a private Servex+SERVEX_HOME: 'Add Dark Mode Toggle' (p-9) then 'Actually put that toggle in the settings panel, not the top bar' (p-10) reused the SAME card id `c-add-dark-mode-toggle` with route:"correction" — a genuine same-idea-different-words continuation, not a coincidental id collision.

Deliverable 5 (selection-aware routing): compose.js now sends `selected: <card id>` alongside `re` on every prompt (typed and whisper); assistant.md tells the assistant that id is the DEFAULT and it may file elsewhere when a sentence plainly is not about it. PROVEN: with selected=c-login-form, 'card A is the login form, keep working on it' evolved id c-login-form; the NEXT sentence 'look at the payment page instead, that's broken' (same selected) correctly minted a NEW card c-payment-page-broken instead, saying in its own text 'this replaces the login form as the priority'. The visual re-route caveat/one-click-undo on the CARD ITSELF is not built — that lives in ai2/card.js and inbox.js, both outside this task's fence (owned by inbox-model).

Deliverable 6 (mention links): Assistant.js reads real page.js `title:` fields (new Page/Doc({...title...}) only, not any title: deeper in the file) and wraps ONE matching mention per text in a markdown link, applied to card.title and refined.text. PROVEN: 'AI 2 dashboard'->[AI 2](/framework/ai2/), 'the grip'->[Grip](/framework/ext/grip/), 'the talk page'->[Talk](/framework/ai/talk/), all three urls verified live. talk/page.js's TalkCard.headline() now uses .md() instead of .text() so the link actually renders (screenshot: talk-1280-done.png, no layout break).

REAL BUG found and fixed before it shipped: my first linkify() implementation matched titles inside the site's own deep test-fixture tree (core/new/1/site/patterns/, core/Page/old/, styles/layouts/), which is full of demo pages reusing ordinary English words as titles (four different pages titled 'Dashboard'). A sentence containing both 'AI 2' and 'dashboard' picked the longer, WRONG match ('Dashboard', pointing at a fixture 90 chars deep); slugifying that title for a card id, then a task id, then an agent id, produced a name over Log.js's 64-char filename limit and CRASHED the whole Servex process (agent host down, ECONNREFUSED). Fixed by scoping titles() to real top-level module directories only (ext/*, ux/*, ai2, ai/talk) instead of walking all of framework/ — 36 safe titles instead of hundreds of fixture ones. Second, separate bug in the same function: looping title-by-title and replacing INTO the growing string let a later title's regex match text INSIDE a link this function itself had just inserted (`/ext/Ask/`'s own path contains the word 'Ext') producing doubly-nested corrupted markdown. Fixed: scan the untouched original text once, take the single longest match across all titles, write exactly one link.

REAL BUG found and fixed: MasterAssistant's own `id` ("assistant-master") did not match what Agents.spawn()'s name() actually mints from {role:"master-assistant", name:"master"} ("master-assistant-master"), so live() could never find the session it had just spawned — every single prompt spawned a BRAND NEW Claude session from scratch (7 separate sessions observed for 12 prompts, each paying its own ~$0.09-0.10 boot cost). Fixed by setting id to the id Agents.name() actually mints. Re-tested with 10 more prompts: one session reused throughout, cost measured at $0.226/10 prompts (over the $0.10 budget-mode ceiling — throttling to every-other-prompt kicked in and logged correctly), master stayed silent except two `refined` summaries (one per five prompts, exactly as specified) and zero disputes (correctly agreed with the fast assistant throughout).

CAUTION for future proofs against a real Servex instance: a `route:"task"` card feeds Servex's own Dispatcher, which spawns a REAL task-mastermind agent that does real file reads (and, per its own skill, could write) in the worktree it runs from — unrelated to this task's own SERVEX_HOME isolation, which only isolates Servex's ports/logs, not the Dispatcher's own spawned agents' cwd. Two of my early test sentences ('AI 2 dashboard', 'fix the grip jitter') accidentally triggered two of these. Both were caught (one did a harmless read-only report and stopped; the other's directory was empty, killed before it wrote anything) and cleaned up — the one real ai/2026-09-22/day.jsonl line it wrote was removed, restoring the file exactly; two empty/harmless untracked task dirs were rm -rf'd. Future proofs against a live Dispatcher should phrase test sentences as notes/questions, not build requests, or set whatever env flag disables Dispatcher.dispatch (not chased down here — time).

Owner addenda arrived mid-task (19:45, 19:50, 19:55) adding items 7-12. Items 7-8 (typed `reply` within seconds of a card-directed sentence; the tool-arg-arrives-as-a-JSON-string bug producing `undefined-` ids) are in this task's own fence (assistant.md + Assistant.js) and are FIXED: both Assistant classes now unwrap a stringified `event` arg before minting, drop (and count) anything still typeless rather than writing garbage; assistant.md adds a `reply` event type. PROVEN: a card-directed 'Hello, can you hear me?' got a typed reply ('Yes, loud and clear.', re: the card id) landing ~5s later — a bit over the owner's 2-3s target, which reads as normal LLM turn latency in this environment (observed 4-9s per turn throughout this session) rather than a wiring bug.

assign.outcome: Open-mic mode landed: Dictate.js gets `mode:"open"` (mic stays on indefinitely, box never written into, settled sentences append as their own lines) wired into `talk` and AI 2's composer. The fast assistant now takes a `correction` route and can evolve an earlier card by id, reads a `selected` card to default to and can override it when a sentence is plainly about something else, and links known page mentions ('AI 2 dashboard', 'the grip', 'the talk page') into real, resolving urls in card titles and refined text. A second, always-alive master assistant (Sonnet, budget mode) listens to every prompt, stays silent unless it disagrees or a thread earns a summary (at most 1 per 5), and throttles itself once its own cost passes $0.10 per 10 prompts. Two real bugs the owner had already found live (a stringified tool-call arg producing `undefined-` ids, and card-directed sentences getting no reply) are fixed in the same files. Two more bugs surfaced only by testing this build against a real Servex — a crash from linking to the site's own deep test-fixture titles, and the master assistant respawning a brand-new session on every prompt instead of staying alive — were found and fixed before landing, not shipped. Proven live: three real whisper segments through the open mic with an empty, enabled box and zero console errors; a same-topic-different-words sentence evolving one card, not three; a selected card correctly overridden when a sentence was about something else; three mention-links resolving 200; the master assistant's real cost measured and its throttle firing. Left for the mastermind: items 9-12 of the mid-task addenda (mic-color CSS, AI 2's rail composer + a page.js checkbox, an inbox.js archive feature) touch two other minions' owned files and are logged as a deferred decision, not built here.

log.msg: Item 9 done: Dictate.js's button icon is now a child span beside a new .ux-dictate-level bar, both inheriting --ux-dictate-level (unchanged, still set every audio frame). Listening = a solid, static box-shadow ring in --prim (no more box-shadow sized by loudness, no more pulse animation on the button itself); only the level bar moves. Applies everywhere Dictate mounts (one shared component) - proven on talk and AI 2's card composer with on/off screenshots at 1280; not individually re-shot on the other 5 mounts (v/3, ext/Ask, AITask, assistant-stream) since the fix lives entirely in the shared Dictate.js/css, not per-mount code.

Item 10 done: composer({mic:false}) skips building ComposerMic and the popover entirely - used for AI 2's top rail composer (now typed-only, Send still starts a new card). A card's own page keeps its own mic, one per card. A remembered 'auto-transcribe' checkbox (localStorage, default on) sits beside + New card; card_page's autostart now reads it (autostart: fresh && auto_transcribe()). Proven: rail_mic_count=0, checkbox defaults checked, a new card's own mic auto-starts and shows listening.

Item 11: reverted after live testing showed a real risk, not shipped. My first attempt (a longer 'paragraph pause' that only forces a cut when the guess-so-far does not yet end in . ? or !) relies on the last periodic whisper resend (up to 1.5s stale) to judge 'ends a sentence' - tested against a 3-repeat clip with 900ms gaps, it MERGED all three into what looked like one continuous segment instead of three, exactly the regression the whole open-mic feature depends on NOT having. Reverted to the original 700ms-flat pause_ms (unchanged from what already landed). The owner's original mid-sentence-break complaint is real but needs a sturdier fix (e.g. forcing a fresh transcribe the instant a pause starts, not trusting the last periodic one) that this session did not have the budget to build and prove safely - logged as a follow-up, not silently dropped.

Item 12 done: items()  in inbox.js now returns the visible list with an extra `.archived` array property (status:archived items, same shape) instead of dropping them outright. page.js adds an 'archived (n)' word at the rail's foot (hidden at 0) that toggles them back into the SAME list, greyed via .ai2-archived (opacity .45) rather than a second view. inbox.js exports archive_card(id), the same board-append + local-offset stamp() new_card() uses; card.js's full() gets a small 'clear' button next to the flag, wired to on.clear in card_page. + New card's own `at` now uses the same local-offset stamp() instead of .toISOString() (the other half of the mixed-clock bug). Proven: archived (n) count tracks live, clicking it shows the greyed rows, clear on a real test card moved it there, and reload (a fresh page.goto) kept it archived.

Bonus, in-fence now that ai2/** is open: card.js's full() switched its title/refined .text() calls to .md() so a link the fast assistant already wraps in markdown (open-mic's item 6, landed earlier today) actually renders as a clickable link in AI 2 too, not just on the talk page.

Process note: this session's scratchpad moved (worktree torn down -> main tree) mid-task without me noticing at first - my first two proof runs against a stale wav-file path silently got total silence from Chrome's fake audio device (no error, --ux-dictate-level pinned at 0.000 for 8+ straight ticks), which looked exactly like a real regression until traced to the missing file. Re-copied the fixture into the new scratchpad and confirmed the actual mechanism was never broken.

Cost: this session's LLM spend was the fast assistant answering the real prompts posted by these proofs on the live Servex (unavoidable - proving on 8123 means the real assistant hears it) plus the earlier session's own proof work; no new Sonnet/master-assistant fan-out was spawned for items 9-12 (pure UI/CSS/JS, no agent calls of their own). Well under the $10 ceiling.
